profile.summary: MADGEN (Mass-spec Attends to De Novo Molecular GENeration) generates molecular structures from a tandem mass spectrum in two stages. First it retrieves the molecule's core scaffold (its Murcko ring framework) by ranking candidate scaffolds against the spectrum; then a spectrum-guided generative model adds the remaining atoms and bonds, using the chemical formula to fix which atoms are present. It outputs sampled candidate molecules.

summary_quotes.text: a scaffold-based method for de novo molecular structure generation guided by mass spectrometry data. MADGEN operates in two stages: scaffold retrieval and spectra-conditioned molecular generation starting with the scaffold.
Since the atom set V can be directly inferred from the chemical formula, the task of molecular generation involves determining the appropriate edge set

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Stage 1 treats scaffold retrieval as ranking: contrastive learning aligns spectra (with their formula) with candidate Murcko scaffolds, and the top-ranked scaffold is chosen; an oracle retriever that is given the true scaffold is used to measure stage 2 alone. Stage 2 starts from the scaffold and the formula's atoms and generates the missing bonds with a Markov bridge process adapted from RetroBridge, using attention to bring spectral information into every step. The generator is a 5-layer graph transformer. The paper gives 50 diffusion steps in one passage and a 100-step Markov bridge in its training details; the README samples with --n_steps 100.

quotes.text: we formulate scaffold retrieval as a ranking problem and employ contrastive learning to align mass spectra with candidate molecular scaffolds.
RetroBridge is adapted for MADGEN’s second step, where we aim to model the joint distribution of scaffolds and target molecules
starting from the retrieved scaffold, we employ the MS/MS spectrum to guide an attention-based generative model to generate the final molecule.
The model was trained using a graph transformer with 5 layers and 50 diffusion steps.
A Markov bridge process with 100 steps is employed during training

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two pretrained generators are released on Zenodo record 17115068 (CC-BY-4.0): msgym.ckpt (MassSpecGym) and canopus.ckpt (CANOPUS), together with processed data, predicted scaffold rankings and scaffold-retrieval datasets. The NIST23 model and data are not public because NIST is licensed. The paper read is arXiv v4 (29 Apr 2025), published at ICLR 2025. A result should say whether the predictive or the oracle scaffold retriever was used, because the gap is large.

sections.title: Use in the benchmark source
sections.body: MassSpecGym in the Wild (an existing source on this record) lists MADGEN in its updated MassSpecGym de novo leaderboard with 1.31% top-1 accuracy, the same figure the MADGEN paper reports for MassSpecGym with its predictive scaffold retriever.

quotes.text: the predictive retriever yields a top-1 accuracy of 4.6%, while for CANOPUS and MassSpecGym, the top-1 accuracies is 2.10 % and 1.31%.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Two-stage de novo structure generator from MS/MS: contrastive scaffold retrieval plus spectrum-conditioned graph generation.

quotes.text: MADGEN operates in two stages: scaffold retrieval and spectra-conditioned molecular generation starting with the scaffold.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Contrastive scaffold ranker; graph transformer generator (5 layers; the paper gives 50 diffusion steps in one passage and a 100-step Markov bridge in its training details) with a Markov bridge from scaffold to molecule and attention over the spectrum.

quotes.text: a graph transformer with 5 layers and 50 diffusion steps.
RetroBridge is adapted for MADGEN’s second step
A Markov bridge process with 100 steps is employed during training

strengths.text: With the true scaffold given (oracle retriever) the authors report top-1 accuracy of 49.0% on NIST23, 18.7% on CANOPUS and 10.5% on MassSpecGym (the authors' figures), showing the generator works when the scaffold is right.

quotes.text: On NIST23, MADGEN achieves a top-1 accuracy of 49.0% and a top-10 accuracy of 65.5%

strengths.text: MIT code and CC-BY-4.0 checkpoints and data for MassSpecGym and CANOPUS.
The scaffold stage gives partial structural information (the molecular backbone) even when the full structure is wrong.

quotes.text: can provide partial insight in regard to the molecular backbone of the measured spectra.

limitations.text: End-to-end accuracy is limited by scaffold retrieval: with the predictive retriever, top-1 accuracy is 2.10% on CANOPUS and 1.31% on MassSpecGym (the authors' figures).

quotes.text: the low scaffold prediction accuracy of the predictive retriever constrains molecular generation performance.

limitations.text: Needs the chemical formula, which fixes the atom set.

quotes.text: Since the atom set V can be directly inferred from the chemical formula

run_guide.summary: Install MADGEN, download the processed MassSpecGym data and the MassSpecGym checkpoint, and sample candidate molecules for the test set.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/HassounLab/MADGEN.git
cd MADGEN
git checkout --detach 0099dcbd34cb177b493b177537bf41f6e3f3b41c
steps.explanation: Clone and pin the reviewed commit; these lines are added by Rewire.

quotes.text: Our code is available at https://github.com/HassounLab/MADGEN

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
conda create --name madgen python=3.9 rdkit=2023.09.5 -c conda-forge -y
conda activate madgen
pip install -r requirements.txt

quotes.text: conda create --name madgen python=3.9 rdkit=2023.09.5 -c conda-forge -y conda activate madgen

steps.title: Download the checkpoint
steps.explanation: The README links the checkpoint record but gives no download command.

quotes.text: Pre-trained model checkpoints are available at:

steps.title: Sample molecules
steps.shell:
python sample.py \
    --config configs/msgym.yaml \
    --checkpoint {checkpoint_path} \
    --samples samples \
    --model Madgen \
    --mode test \
    --n_samples 50 \
    --n_steps 100 \
    --table_name {table_name} \
    --sampling_seed 42
steps.explanation: The README's sampling template with the dataset set to msgym; replace {checkpoint_path} with the downloaded msgym.ckpt and {table_name} with an output name. The README prefixes it with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1.

quotes.text: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python sample.py \ --config configs/{dataset_name}.yaml \ --checkpoint {checkpoint_path} \ --samples samples \ --model Madgen \ --mode test \ --n_samples 50 \ --n_steps 100 \ --table_name {table_name} \ --sampling_seed 42

outputs: A results table of generated SMILES; python evaluation_generation.py --file_path <csv> computes top-K accuracy, maximum Tanimoto similarity and scaffold coverage.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
Whether sampling uses predicted scaffolds or needs the scaffold-retrieval step first (scaffold_retrieval/ and preprocess_rank.py) is not stated clearly in the README.
